The Formats and Integrity Edition — a new lossless reordering mode, library presets that match
nf-core/methylseq, and a run that now either writes a complete file or writes nothing.

- **New `--clump_only` mode** ([#353](https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/issues/353)) — reorders FASTQ records by canonical 16-mer minimizer for gzip-friendly compression, with no trimming, filtering or adapter detection, and records byte-identical to the input.
- **`--library <preset>` names a library prep instead of four clip flags** ([#440](https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/issues/440)) — `emseq`, `accel`, `zymo`, `scbs` and `pbat` expand to the same clip values nf-core/methylseq uses, so both routes trim identically.
- **Breaking: `--fastqc` is refused on the four specialty modes, and on `--paired` with a single interleaved uBAM writing FASTQ** ([#421](https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/issues/421)) — those paths write no report, so the flag now fails loudly rather than being silently ignored.
- **An output file is published only if every byte it owes was written** ([#434](https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/issues/434)) — a disk error in a run's last few bytes previously left a trailerless `.gz` at its final name and exited 0.
- **`--phred64` is checked against the input before anything is written** ([#532](https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/issues/532)) — a mislabelled Phred+64 file is refused up front, which means some runs that previously completed are now refused.
- **The bundled FastQC engine moves to Java FastQC 0.13.0, clearing 19 security advisories** ([#500](https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/issues/500)) — reports gain `Mean Length` and `Median Length`; MultiQC parses the old and new shapes without warnings.

Full record, including every bug fix and dependency bump:
[CHANGELOG, Version 2.4.0](https://www.trimgalore.com/reference/changelog/).

## Install

```bash
cargo install trim-galore
conda install -c bioconda trim-galore
docker pull ghcr.io/felixkrueger/trimgalore:latest
```
